title: Homotopically projective dg-module replacements and enhanced localization
statement:
Fix universes as in [def-weil-size-convention], enlarged to contain the module categories used here. Let $\mathcal B$ be a small dg category over $\mathbf Z$: every $\mathcal B(U,V)$ is a cochain complex, composition is a unital associative chain map, and a cochain differential has degree $1$ and square zero. A right dg module consists of complexes $M(U)$ with unital associative chain-map actions $M(V)\otimes\mathcal B(U,V)\to M(U)$. Write $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathcal B}(M,N)$ for the complex whose degree-$r$ elements are degree-$r$ maps of graded right modules (so $f(ma)=f(m)a$), with differential $df=d_Nf-(-1)^rf d_M$. A module is objectwise acyclic if all its cohomology groups at every object vanish; a module map is an objectwise quasi-isomorphism if it induces isomorphisms on these cohomology groups. Call $Q$ homotopically projective if $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathcal B}(Q,N)$ is acyclic whenever $N$ is objectwise acyclic.

Every right dg module $M$ admits an objectwise quasi-isomorphism $q_M:QM\to M$ with $QM$ homotopically projective. The full dg category of homotopically projective modules, with the displayed Hom complexes and composition of graded maps, presents the enhanced localization of right dg modules at objectwise quasi-isomorphisms. Here enhanced localization retains the derived complexes of maps and their homotopy coherent compositions, rather than only the category with morphisms $H^0$. For a homotopically projective module $Q$ and any module $M$, the complex $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathcal B}(Q,M)$ represents the derived mapping complex from $Q$ to $M$. These identifications are compatible with composition and with the localization functor. An objectwise quasi-isomorphism between homotopically projective modules is a chain homotopy equivalence, meaning it has a closed degree-zero inverse up to boundaries in the Hom complexes. In particular equivalence of such modules in the enhanced localization is the same as isomorphism in the category whose morphisms are $H^0$ of these Hom complexes.

proof.text: For each right dg module $M$, apply the semi-free replacement statement to obtain $q_M:QM\to M$, with a countable exhaustive filtration starting at zero, graded-split inclusions and shifted-representable successor quotients. This supplies the replacements used below; it requires no boundedness, flatness or projectivity of the complexes $\mathcal B(U,V)$.

proof.text: Apply the semi-free homotopical-projectivity statement to the filtration of $QM$. Thus $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathcal B}(QM,N)$ is acyclic for every objectwise acyclic $N$, which is exactly the condition defining homotopical projectivity in the item. This supplies the first assertion.

source.place: Section 14.8; dg-algebra prototype Stacks tag 09KM, label dga-lemma-property-P-K-projective.

proof.text: For a closed degree-zero map $s:N\to N\prime$, its cone has $C(s)^r=N\prime{}^r\oplus N^{r+1}$ and differential $(y,x)\mapsto(dy+s(x),-dx)$. If $s$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $(y,x)$ is a cone cocycle, injectivity on cohomology gives $x=dz$; subtracting $d(0,-z)=(-s(z),dz)$ leaves $(y+s(z),0)$. Surjectivity gives a cycle $w$ and $b$ with $y+s(z)=s(w)+db$, so this remainder is $d(b,w)$. Conversely, acyclicity of the cone applied to $(y,0)$ for a target cycle gives $y=db+s(a)$ with $da=0$, proving surjectivity; applied to $(-y,x)$ when $dx=0$ and $s(x)=dy$, it gives $x=-da$, proving injectivity. Thus its cone is objectwise acyclic precisely when $s$ is an objectwise quasi-isomorphism. Applying the graded Hom definition gives $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathcal B}(Q,C(s))=C(\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathcal B}(Q,s))$: in degree $r$ both sides consist of pairs of maps of degrees $r$ and $r+1$, with the same displayed cone differential. If $Q$ is homotopically projective this cone is acyclic, so Hom from $Q$ preserves objectwise quasi-isomorphisms.

source.place: Cone calculation; compare tag 09KY, label dga-lemma-hom-derived, proof.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal C$ be the full dg category of right dg $\mathcal B$-modules with module values in a fixed universe, enlarging once more to make this category small, and let $\mathcal A$ be its full subcategory of objectwise acyclic modules. Zero, shifts and cones are computed objectwise, so both are pretriangulated and $\mathcal A$ is closed under shifts and cones. By step 3, the maps with cone in $\mathcal A$ are precisely the objectwise quasi-isomorphisms. Apply the generic dg-quotient statement: $j:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C/\mathcal A$ therefore presents the enhanced localization. For homotopically projective $Q$, the left $\mathcal A$-module $h^Q(N)=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathcal B}(Q,N)$ is objectwise acyclic. It is thus equivalent to the zero module, and the derived tensor $h_M\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal A}h^Q$ is zero. The cofiber sequence now says that the canonical map $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathcal B}(Q,M)\to(\mathcal C/\mathcal A)(jQ,jM)$ is an equivalence in $\mathbf D(\mathbf Z)$. This computes the derived mapping complex; underived tensor exactness over $\mathbf Z$ is not assumed.

Restrict the quotient map $j$ to the full dg category $\mathcal P$ of homotopically projective modules. Step 4 gives equivalences on every mapping object, so this functor is fully faithful with its derived enrichment. For every module $M$, steps 1-2 supply $QM\in\mathcal P$ and the inverted map $j(q_M):j(QM)\simeq j(M)$, so it is essentially surjective. By the fully faithful and essentially surjective criterion in dg-enrichment rectification, $\mathcal P$ presents the enhanced localization. The comparison maps are restrictions of the single enriched quotient functor $j$. Explicitly, on $\operatorname{Hom}(Q\prime,Q\prime\prime)\otimes^{\mathbf L}\operatorname{Hom}(Q,Q\prime)$, composing first in $\mathcal C$ and then applying its mapping-object comparison agrees with applying the two comparisons first and then composing in $\mathcal C/\mathcal A$; this is the enriched-functor composition axiom for $j$. Its unit axiom takes the identity class of $Q$ to that of $jQ$, and its coherent functor structure supplies the corresponding compatibility for all higher compositions. These are statements in the derived enrichment; no strict enriched replacement functor or cochain-level representative of the quotient functor is assumed. Naturality in an arbitrary target $M$ is the naturality of the cofiber comparison of step 4. Thus these identifications preserve composition, units and all coherent composition data, and agree with the localization functor.

source.place: Section 1.3.2-1.3.3 and 1.6; enriched interpretation through the existing rectification statement.

proof.text: Let $u:Q\to Q\prime$ be an objectwise quasi-isomorphism with both modules homotopically projective. Step 3 with source $Q\prime$ gives a bijection $H^0\operatorname{Hom}(Q\prime,Q)\to H^0\operatorname{Hom}(Q\prime,Q\prime)$ by postcomposition with $u$. Lift $[1_{Q\prime}]$ to a class represented by a closed degree-zero $v:Q\prime\to Q$; then $uv-1_{Q\prime}=dh\prime$ for a degree-$-1$ map $h\prime$. Step 3 with source $Q$ makes postcomposition with $u$ injective on $H^0\operatorname{Hom}(Q,Q)$. Since $u(vu-1_Q)=(uv-1_{Q\prime})u=d(h\prime u)$, injectivity gives $vu-1_Q=dh$ for a degree-$-1$ map $h$. Thus $v$ is a chain homotopy inverse. Conversely these boundary equations imply inverse cohomology maps. By step 5 and the rectification statement identifying the underlying homotopy category with $H^0$, any equivalence between such modules is an isomorphism in their $H^0$ category, and every such isomorphism yields an equivalence.

lean.statement: theorem exists_projective_enhancement (B : IntegralDGCategory.{u, v}) : ∃ D : ModuleDGModel.{u, v, w} B, (∀ M : Ordinary D.dg, ∃ (Q : Ordinary D.dg) (q : Q ⟶ M), D.IsProjective (ForgetEnrichment.to Complex.{max u v w + 1} Q) ∧ D.weakEquivalences q) ∧ (∀ (Q M N : Ordinary D.dg) (f : M ⟶ N), D.IsProjective (ForgetEnrichment.to Complex.{max u v w + 1} Q) → D.weakEquivalences f → QuasiIso (postcompose Q f)) ∧ (∀ (Q Q' : Ordinary D.dg) (q : Q ⟶ Q'), D.IsProjective (ForgetEnrichment.to Complex.{max u v w + 1} Q) → D.IsProjective (ForgetEnrichment.to Complex.{max u v w + 1} Q') → D.weakEquivalences q → D.HasHomotopyInverse q) ∧ D.PresentsEnhancedLocalization
lean.note: The canonical full dg-module enrichment is specified in all integer degrees by bijections to the recorded graded-module maps, with exact differential, unit, composition and evaluation normalizations. Its literal full projective subcategory, the recorded Dold–Kan realization and coherent nerve, and the full coherent-functor localization property give a concrete dg presentation of the enhanced localization. The derived-Hom comparison is canonical postcomposition along replacement quasi-isomorphisms. Independent input universes are enlarged to a common bound, without flatness or boundedness assumptions. Added statement dependencies already have landed interfaces; the rectification theorem remains proof-only.
